question: Let $P = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 0\\2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $Q = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\0 & 2\end{bmatrix}$. Compute $(P'Q - Q'P)'$ and then deduce whether the resulting matrix is symmetric, skew symmetric, or neither, providing full justification.
explanation:
First compute the transposes:

$P' = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 2\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $Q' = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $P'Q$:

$P'Q = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 2\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\0 & 2\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 1\\0 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $Q'P$:

$Q'P = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0\\2 & 1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 0\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.

Thus $P'Q - Q'P = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\-1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$.

Taking transpose:

$(P'Q - Q'P)' = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$.

Since $(P'Q - Q'P)' = -(P'Q - Q'P)$, the matrix is skew symmetric.

options.D: $(P'Q-Q'P)'=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\0&2\end{bmatrix}$, and it is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric.
